# AU Corporate

> AU Corporate is a CA-led firm that handles company incorporation and registration in India, serving clients across all Indian states and union territories, and foreign parent companies from more than 10 countries. Founded in 2016 and led by Chartered Accountant Abhishek Jaiin (ICAI 544646), it registers private limited companies, wholly owned subsidiaries, LLPs and branch, liaison and project offices, then runs their accounting, FEMA/RBI filings, tax, transfer pricing, company secretarial compliance and payroll. Serving clients across India, with its head office in New Delhi.

Primary services: India market entry and Global Capability Center (GCC) advisory, assurance and accounting (IFRS/Ind AS), taxation and transfer pricing, FEMA and RBI regulatory compliance, monthly accounting and payroll, Virtual CFO services, HR and payroll services, risk and transaction advisory, business valuation, and arbitration/dispute resolution.

Service area: all of India, with clients worldwide. Subsidiary registration: USD 750 to 1,000 all-inclusive; incorporation typically takes 4 to 6 weeks.

Contact: partner@theaucorp.com | +91-9999010513 | Serving clients across India

Full page index (every page on the site, not just the curated list below): https://www.theaucorp.com/llms-full.txt

## USA → India — Full Resource List

A long-form guide cluster for US companies setting up and running a subsidiary in India, with a section on the India-US tax treaty and social security for US expats:

- [Set Up a Subsidiary in India from the USA: 2026 Guide](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india): How US companies set up a subsidiary in India: structure, FDI rules, incorporation steps, RBI/FEMA filings, tax and compliance. By a Chartered Accountant.
- [Tax and Social Security Treaties for US Companies in India](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties): The India-US tax treaty (DTAA) and social security for US expats: treaty rates, residency, EPF, FICA and the missing totalization agreement.
- [Treaty and Social Security FAQs for India-US Expats](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/faq): 50 plain answers on the India-US tax treaty, DTAA withholding rates, Form 6166 and 41, expat tax, EPF, FICA and the missing totalization agreement.
- [India-US DTAA: Tax Treaty Between the US and India Explained](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/india-us-dtaa-guide): How the India-US tax treaty works: who qualifies, which taxes it covers, how treaty and domestic law interact, residency, relief from double tax and disputes.
- [India-US DTAA Withholding Tax Rates for Payments to the US](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/dtaa-withholding-rates): Treaty rates for payments from India to the US: dividends 15% or 25%, interest 10% or 15%, royalties and fees 10% or 15%. Conditions and how to apply them.
- [EPF for International Workers in India: Rules for US Expats](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/epf-international-workers): How Indian provident fund applies to foreign nationals: international worker rules, no wage ceiling, withdrawal, court rulings and the 2026 EPF Scheme.
- [Claiming India-US Treaty Benefits: Form 6166 and Form 41](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/treaty-benefits-documents): Documents needed to claim India-US treaty rates: IRS Form 6166, Form 41 (previously Form 10F), no-PE declaration and beneficial ownership.
- [Tax Residency for US Expats in India: Treaty and Credits](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/expat-tax-residency-india-us): Which country taxes a US expat in India: Indian residency tests, US worldwide tax, the treaty tie-breaker, foreign tax credit and exclusion.
- [US-India Totalization Agreement: Social Security for Expats](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/social-security-us-expats-india): Is there a US-India social security agreement? What applies to a US expat in India: provident fund, US FICA, double coverage and planning.
- [US Social Security (FICA) for Americans Working in India](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-and-social-security-treaties/us-social-security-for-americans-in-india): When Social Security and Medicare tax apply to Americans working in India: US employer, Indian subsidiary, Section 3121(l) agreements and self-employment.
- [Global VAT for US Companies Selling Abroad](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/global-vat): How VAT works for US companies selling digital services and goods into Europe, the UK and beyond: registration, B2B and B2C rules and compliance.
- [Audit of a US Company's Indian Subsidiary and ICOFR](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/audit-icofr): Statutory audit, tax audit, GST audit and internal controls over financial reporting for an Indian subsidiary of a US group. What to expect and how to prepare.
- [10 Common Mistakes US Companies Make Setting Up in India](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/common-mistakes): The ten most common and costly mistakes US companies make when setting up an Indian subsidiary, and how to avoid each. Includes a pre-filing checklist.
- [India Subsidiary Compliance Calendar for US Companies](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/compliance-calendar): The recurring compliance of an Indian subsidiary: monthly, quarterly, annual and event-based filings under company, tax, GST, FEMA and labour law.
- [Contracts and Arbitration in India for US Companies](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/contracts-and-arbitration): Intercompany and customer contracts for an Indian subsidiary, governing law, arbitration clauses, the New York Convention and enforcing awards in India.
- [Documents and Apostille for an India Subsidiary (US Parent)](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/documents-and-apostille): Which documents a US parent must prepare to incorporate an Indian subsidiary, and how notarization and apostille work for US state and federal documents.
- [India-US Tax Treaty and Permanent Establishment Risk](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/dtaa-pe-risk): How the India-US tax treaty applies to payments to your US parent: Withholding Tax rates, Tax Residency Certificate, Form 41 and permanent establishment risk.
- [EOR vs Subsidiary in India: Which Is Right for a US Company?](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/eor-vs-subsidiary): Compare an Employer of Record with your own Indian subsidiary: speed, control, compliance, tax presence and when to convert. A guide for US companies.
- [ESOPs for Indian Employees of a US Parent Company](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/esop): How ESOPs and RSUs work for employees of an Indian subsidiary: FEMA reporting, employee tax, valuation, cost recharge and transfer pricing for a US parent.
- [Sending a US Executive to India: Visa, Housing and Tax](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/expat-visa): How to relocate a US executive to India: employment visa, FRRO registration, housing, banking, tax residency and permanent establishment risk for the parent.
- [216 FAQs: Setting Up an India Subsidiary from the USA](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/faq): 216 plain answers for US companies: incorporation, FEMA, tax, hiring, compliance, repatriation, ESOPs, M&A and closing an Indian subsidiary.
- [Funding an Indian Subsidiary: FEMA and Form FC-GPR](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/funding-fema-fc-gpr): How a US parent invests in an Indian subsidiary: equity, CCPS, ECB, the 60-day allotment rule, pricing, and RBI reporting through Form FC-GPR on FIRMS.
- [Hiring in India: Contracts, Payroll and Statutory Compliance](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/hiring-and-payroll): How US companies hire in India: employment contracts, provident fund, ESI, gratuity, professional tax, payroll steps and India's labour codes.
- [Incorporation Process for an Indian Subsidiary, Step by Step](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/incorporation-process): The eight steps to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary in India from the USA: forms, order of steps, typical 4 to 6 week timeline and first 90 days.
- [Repatriating Profits from India to the US: Forms and Tax](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/repatriating-profits): How a US parent receives money from its Indian subsidiary: dividends, service fees, royalties, loans. Forms 145 and 146, Withholding Tax and DTAA relief.
- [Resident Director Requirement for an Indian Company](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/resident-director): Every Indian company needs a Resident Director who has stayed in India 182 days in the financial year. Who qualifies, options for US parents, and duties.
- [Restructuring, Mergers and Exit for an Indian Subsidiary](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/restructuring-and-exit): Options to restructure, sell, merge or close an Indian subsidiary: share sale, slump sale, merger, buyback, strike-off and liquidation, with tax and RBI steps.
- [Share Valuation for Foreign Investment in India](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/share-valuation): Why shares issued to a US parent need a valuation, who can certify it, the pricing floor under FEMA, and when you need a fresh valuation.
- [Subsidiary vs Branch vs Liaison Office vs LLP in India](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/subsidiary-vs-branch-vs-liaison-office-vs-llp): Compare the four ways a US company can enter India: wholly owned subsidiary, branch office, liaison office and LLP. Activities, approvals, tax and control.
- [Handling Indian Tax Notices for a US-Owned Subsidiary](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/tax-notices-and-litigation): What to do on receiving an Indian income tax, GST or transfer pricing notice: first steps, appeal routes, DRP, ITAT, MAP and Advance Pricing Agreements.
- [Transfer Pricing in India for US-Owned Subsidiaries](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/transfer-pricing): How transfer pricing works for an Indian subsidiary of a US company: arm's length pricing, documentation, Form 48, methods, safe harbour and audits.
- [US Reporting for an Indian Subsidiary: Form 5471, FBAR](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/us-parent-obligations): US reporting that follows when you own an Indian subsidiary: Form 5471, FBAR, Form 8938 and international tax regimes. A guide for US finance teams.
- [Choosing an Indian State and City for a US Company: Talent, Cost, Rules and Incentives](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/choosing-an-indian-state-and-city-for-us-companies): How to choose the state and city for the registered office and the team: a decision framework, a comparison table of major hubs by function, how state law changes stamp duty, professional tax and shops rules, what GIFT City offers, and the order of questions that matter most.
- [Cost of Setting Up a Subsidiary in India from the US: Budget Framework and Fee Questions](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/cost-of-setting-up-a-subsidiary-in-india-from-the-us): A budgeting guide for US companies: what the one-time set-up costs, what the subsidiary costs every year to keep compliant, how to size the capital you invest, and a template and question list for comparing quotes. The AU Corporate set-up fee is stated; other lines are framed so you can build your own estimate.
- [FCPA, Indian Anti-Bribery Law and US Export Controls for an Indian Subsidiary](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/fcpa-anti-bribery-and-export-controls-for-indian-subsidiaries): The compliance rules that follow US law into India: how the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act reaches an Indian subsidiary and its agents, how Indian anti-corruption law applies, a practical programme, export control rules on technology shared with an Indian team, and sanctions screening.
- [Global Capability Centre in India for US Companies: Models, Transfer Pricing and Setup](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/gcc-for-us-companies): How a US company builds a captive engineering, finance or operations centre in India: the three delivery models, entity and tax choices, cost-plus transfer pricing and safe harbour questions, permanent establishment, intellectual property, state incentives and a 12-month roadmap.
- [How Long It Takes to Set Up an Indian Subsidiary from the US: Timeline and Time Zones](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/how-long-it-takes-to-set-up-from-the-us): A schedule for a US parent: US documents and apostille, Indian incorporation, bank onboarding across a 9.5 to 12.5 hour time difference, remittance and the 60-day and 30-day deadlines, plus what to do when a customer deadline forces speed.
- [India's Labour Codes for US Employers: Wages, Notice, Termination and Working Hours](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/indian-labour-codes-for-us-employers): What a US company used to at-will employment needs to know about India's consolidated labour codes: the wage definition and its effect on provident fund and gratuity, fixed-term contracts, the 300-worker threshold for retrenchment permission, working hours, overtime, social security and a practical checklist.
- [Who Owns the Work? IP Assignment, Copyright and Patent Filing Rules for Indian Teams of US Companies](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/ip-ownership-and-copyright-assignment-for-indian-teams): A guide to making sure the US parent owns what the Indian team creates: employment and assignment contracts, the duration and territory defaults in Indian copyright law, patent inventorship and foreign filing permission under the Patents Act, trade secrets, non-competes, open source and transfer pricing for intellectual property.
- [NRI and OCI Founders of US Companies: FEMA Status, Investment Routes and Tax Residency](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/nri-and-oci-founders-of-us-companies-investing-in-india): How the status of the founder changes the plan: how FEMA treats NRIs, OCI cardholders and US citizens of Indian origin, the repatriable and non-repatriable investment routes, whether a US company owned by NRIs is treated differently, resident status for tax, the treaty tie-breaker, directorship and a founder checklist.
- [US Manufacturers in India: PLI, Special Economic Zones, Customs Duty and Product Standards](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/us-manufacturers-pli-sez-and-incentives): What a US manufacturer should check before building or contracting a plant in India: how PLI and zone incentives work and what they require, customs and GST on machinery, product standards and quality control orders, land and power, labour rules, tax rate choices and a project checklist.
- [US Privacy Law and India's DPDP Act: HIPAA, CCPA and Offshore Data Teams](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/us-privacy-hipaa-ccpa-and-dpdp): How a US company handles personal data when an Indian subsidiary or vendor processes it: what US federal and state privacy laws require, HIPAA business associate agreements, customer security reviews, how the DPDP Act treats data of people outside India, employee data in both directions and a controls checklist.
- [US SaaS and Digital Sales into India: GST on Online Services, Withholding and Treaty Issues](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/us-saas-and-digital-sales-into-india): How a US software or digital business is taxed when it sells to India without a local entity: GST on online information and database access services, B2B reverse charge, income tax withholding and the royalty question, the abolition of the equalisation levy, significant economic presence and when to add a local company.
- [US Tax on an Indian Subsidiary: NCTI (Formerly GILTI), Subpart F, Section 245A and Foreign Tax Credits](https://www.theaucorp.com/usa-to-india/us-tax-on-indian-subsidiary-ncti-subpart-f-and-foreign-tax-credit): The US side of an Indian subsidiary for a US C corporation or pass-through owner: how profits are taxed when earned or when distributed, what changed after the July 2025 tax act, the role of Indian tax as a credit, check-the-box choices and the forms (5471, 926, 1118, 8992 and 8993).

- [Contracts, Courts and Arbitration for UK Companies in India: English Judgments, LCIA and Indian Courts](https://www.theaucorp.com/uk-to-india/contracts-courts-arbitration): How a UK company should draft contracts with its Indian subsidiary and customers, choose governing law and seat, and enforce English court judgments and arbitral awards in India.
